name: Yellow-Green (Crayola)
lede: Yellow-Green (Crayola) is a pale, yellowish green named in Crayola's own crayon list, qualified in our data to tell it apart from the standard color-wheel hue of the same base name.

sections.title: A crayon name, qualified
sections.body:
Our library records this swatch as named in the Crayola crayon list, via Wikipedia, and calls it an obscure, qualified name rather than one in everyday use [1]. The "(Crayola)" tag in our data separates it from [[yellow-green-color-wheel|Yellow-Green (Color Wheel)]], the standard wheel-position hue of the same base name, which is a far more saturated green [1].

Its closest measured look-alikes are [[pale-olive-green|Pale Olive Green]], read as darker, and [[veronese-green|Veronese Green]], read as duller [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 system's nearest block is light yellow green, about four units from that block's center [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds no painting where this color covers at least one percent of the canvas, as photographed; a close-reading, within-painting lens finds a single trace appearance [2]. That places it rarer than 88 percent of our named colors [2]. A pale, qualified crayon name has little reason to turn up in centuries of oil paintings [2].
